If the return annotation is `"None"` (the string), then `annotation` will be `"None"`.

steps.message: I have completed the task.

The issue was that when a route function had a return annotation of `-> "None"` (as a string), `get_typed_return_annotation` in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` was returning `NoneType` instead of `None`. This could lead to incorrect behavior when the status code is 204 (No Content), as FastAPI might attempt to validate or serialize the return value against `NoneType` instead of treating it as a bodiless response.

I modified `get_typed_return_annotation` to explicitly check if the annotation is the string `"None"` and return `None` in that case. This ensures consistency between `-> None` and `-> "None"`.

I verified the fix with a reproduction script that checked both the return value of `get_typed_return_annotation` and the actual behavior of a FastAPI app with routes using these annotations. Both cases now correctly return `None` and result in a 204 No Content response without a body.
